role: Stochastic identity contract for independent FLEXPART 11.1 oracle realizations. Defines how a requested stochastic realization is identified and produced. Does not execute ensembles, aggregate statistics, or define parity thresholds (owned by issues #57/#58/#59).

oracle_kind_definitions.pristine-oracle: Unmodified FLEXPART 11.1 sources at the pinned commit, built under the frozen #49 execution profile. The normative model reference. Knows no FLEXPART_VALIDATION_SEED handling; setting the variable has no effect on it.
oracle_kind_definitions.seedable-validation-oracle: Pinned FLEXPART 11.1 sources plus exactly the versioned validation-only RNG-initialization patch below, built under the same frozen #49 execution profile. A separately identified validation instrument, never a replacement normative oracle. Must never be reported as pristine-oracle.

native_seed_control_evidence: random_mod.f90 alloc_random hard-codes iseed1(i)=-7-i and iseed2(i)=-88-i with no input path
FLEXPART.f90 hard-codes idummy=-320 for the precomputed Gaussian table
Release-jitter sites hard-code ran1 idummies (-7 in initialise_mod.f90 release_parts, -8/-11 in domain-fill paths, -11 in initdomain_mod.f90)
COMMAND namelist (readoptions_mod.f90) exposes no seed variable
No getenv/get_environment_variable, command_argument, random_seed intrinsic, or random_number intrinsic call exists in the pinned sources

canonical_identity.representation: decimal integer in environment variable FLEXPART_VALIDATION_SEED
notes: 0 is rejected: offset 0 is the pristine default and must stay expressible only as default mode (unset/empty variable), never as a requested identity
Values above 1000000000 are rejected to keep every derived 32-bit Fortran integer seed far from overflow
Non-canonical spellings (blanks, signs, decimal points, trailing text) are rejected instead of being parsed leniently
Leading zeros are rejected: canonical decimal representation has no leading zeros (e.g., '01' is invalid)

derivation_mapping.algorithm_reference: Numerical Recipes ran3 (Knuth subtractive, mbig=1000000000, mseed=161803398, 55-entry table per thread) for iseed1/iseed2 streams; Box-Muller gasdev1 over ran3 thread 0 for the rannumb table; Park-Miller ran1 with Bays-Durham shuffle for release jitter (unpatched, see limitations)

default_mode.semantics: Offset 0: pristine default initialization bit-exactly. A seedable-validation-oracle run in default mode must reproduce the pristine-oracle result to the #49 repeatability criterion, but its oracle_kind stays seedable-validation-oracle.

execution_profile.note: Runtime, build, and Docker boundary come from the frozen #49 contract and are referenced, never duplicated. Thread-count variation is not an acceptable substitute for an explicitly identified stochastic realization.

validation_patch.scope: RNG initialization only: one validation_seed_offset() selector plus its two call sites. RNG algorithms, distributions, call order, OpenMP semantics, and physics are untouched.
validation_patch.application: Applied with git apply to a fresh clone of the pinned pristine checkout; the upstream repository and the pristine checkout are never modified.

rng_namespaces: Candidate Philox seed N and oracle identity N are different RNG namespaces over different generators and must never be equated numerically. Case manifests must keep candidate and oracle stochastic identities structurally separate (see issue #51).
fail_closed: Unsupported or out-of-range stochastic identity is rejected
A missing identity when an independent realization was requested is rejected (S=0 and empty spellings included)
A run whose applied seed/state cannot be proven from its identity record is rejected
A seedable binary whose patch/build identity is unknown is rejected
A seedable run not conforming to the frozen #49 profile is rejected
Provenance labeling a patched executable as pristine-oracle is rejected
Silent fallback from a requested seed to the FLEXPART default seed is rejected (invalid values stop the Fortran run non-zero)
limitations: Release-jitter ran1 streams keep pristine hard-coded idummies; for the point release and single uncertainty class of WIND-UNI-002 they do not influence trajectories (xaux=yaux=zaux=0, nclass 1). Volume releases would need a follow-up.
Convection stream iseed2 is offset for uniformity but unused when LCONVECTION=0 (as in WIND-UNI-002).
Restart files do not persist RNG state; seeded identities apply to fresh runs (IPIN=0).
Single-thread profile only; multi-thread scheduling effects are out of scope by design.
Ten runs justify distinct initialization states, not ensemble statistical adequacy (owned by #57/#58/#59).
